questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 7 AM and 8 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 150 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 hour = 360 ÷ 12 = 30°

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5°

The **minute hand** covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the **minute hand** in 1 minute = 360 ÷ 60 = 6°

__Calculation:__

The time is between **7 AM** and **8 AM** and the required angle is **150 degrees**.

Let the required time be **7:M AM**.

At 7:00, the **hour hand** is at 7 × 30 = 210° (measured from the 12 o'clock position).

Angle of the **hour hand** at 7:M = 210 + 0.5M

Angle of the **minute hand** at 7:M = 6M

The angle between the hands is the absolute difference between their angular positions:

Angle = |(210 + 0.5M) − 6M|

150 = |210 − 5.5M|

**Case 1:**

210 − 5.5M = 150

5.5M = 210 − 150

5.5M = 60

M = 60 ÷ 5.5 ≈ 10.91 minutes

**Case 2:**

210 − 5.5M = −150

5.5M = 210 + 150

5.5M = 360

M = 360 ÷ 5.5 ≈ 65.45 minutes (Since this value exceeds 60 minutes, it falls after 8 AM)

Rounding the value from **Case 1** to the nearest minute, we get **M ≈ 11**.

Thus, the time is approximately **7:11 AM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by the formula:

{Angle} = | (60H - 11M)/(2) |

Where **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

Given **H = 7** and **Angle = 150**.

150 = |(60 × 7 − 11M) ÷ 2|

300 = |420 − 11M|

420 − 11M = 300 ⇒ 11M = 120 ⇒ M = 120 ÷ 11 ≈ 10.91

So, the time is approximately **7:11 AM**.

Therefore, the correct option is 1.

questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 5 AM. The clock gains 1 second every 5 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 5 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

To find the time shown by the clock, we first calculate the **total duration** between the initial time and the target time. Then, we determine the **total gain** based on the given rate of error and add it to the correct time.

__Calculation:__

The clock shows the correct time at **5 AM**.

The time duration from **5 AM** to **5 PM** on the same day = **12 hours**.

Convert the total hours into minutes:

Total minutes = 12 × 60 = **720 minutes**.

It is given that the clock **gains 1 second every 5 minutes**.

Total gain in 720 minutes = 720 ÷ 5

Total gain = **144 seconds**.

Now, convert the gained seconds into minutes and seconds:

144 seconds = (120 + 24) seconds

Since 60 seconds = 1 minute, 120 seconds = 2 minutes.

So, Total gain = **2 minutes and 24 seconds**.

The correct time is **5 PM**. Since the clock is gaining time, it will show:

Time = 5:00:00 + 0:02:24

Time = **5:02:24 PM**

Hence, the clock will show **5:02:24** at 5 PM.

Therefore, the correct answer is **5:02:24**.

questions.question: What is the traditional attire worn by women performing Tippani dance?

options.text: Chaniya choli (traditional skirt and blouse) with ornaments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaniya choli (traditional skirt and blouse) with ornaments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tippani dance** is a vibrant folk dance originating from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, traditionally performed by women from the **Koli** and **Gola** communities.
 
• The performers wear the iconic **Chaniya choli**, which consists of a long, flared skirt called the **Chaniya** (or Ghagra) and a short, fitted blouse known as the **Choli**.
 
• This ethnic ensemble is typically made of brightly colored cotton or silk, often featuring intricate **embroidery**, mirror work, and heavy borders to reflect the cultural heritage of **Gujarat**.
 
• Accompanying the dress, women wear **traditional ornaments** such as heavy silver necklaces, chunky bangles, waistbands (Kandora), and earrings, which provide a rhythmic sound and visual appeal during the dance.
 
• A colorful **Odhni** or dupatta is draped over the head or shoulders, tucked into the waist to allow free movement while beating the **Tippani** sticks against the ground.
 
• Hence, **Chaniya choli (traditional skirt and blouse) with ornaments** is the correct attire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tippani Tool and Origin**:

 
 
• The dance is named after the **Tippani**, a wooden mallet-like tool used by construction workers in **Chorwad** and **Veraval** to level floors.
 
• It transitioned from a labor activity into a folk art where women beat the floor in a rhythmic pattern, often accompanied by instruments like the **Zanj**, **Manjira**, **Tabla**, and **Dhol**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Jewelry**:
 
 
• The **ornaments** are not merely decorative; they signify the marital status and social standing of the women in rural **Gujarati** communities.
 
• In the context of the dance, the **mirror work** on the attire catches the light, creating a shimmering effect that complements the high-energy movements of the dancers.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is rich in which type of soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deccan Plateau** is characterized by its vast stretches of **Black soil**, which is also scientifically referred to as **Regur soil**.
 
• This soil type originates from the weathering and denudation of **basaltic rocks** formed by ancient **volcanic activity** and lava flows during the **Cretaceous period**.
 
• **Black soil** is globally renowned for its high **clay content**, which grants it an exceptional capacity for **moisture retention**, crucial for agriculture in rain-fed areas.
 
• It exhibits a unique **self-ploughing** property; during the dry season, it develops deep **vertical cracks** that facilitate the oxygenation of the soil and internal drainage.
 
• Chemically, it is rich in essential plant nutrients such as **Calcium Carbonate**, **Magnesium**, **Potash**, and **Lime**, although it is typically deficient in **Phosphorous** and **Nitrogen**.
 
• Geographically, it dominates the **North-Western** part of the plateau, covering significant portions of **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and the **Malwa Plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Cotton Soil**:

 
 
• It is primarily used for the cultivation of **Cotton**, earning it the specific nomenclature **Black Cotton Soil**.
 
• Apart from cotton, it supports crops like **Sugarcane**, **Wheat**, **Linseed**, and **Sunflowers**.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil**:
 
 
• Formed by the deposition of silts by the **Himalayan rivers**. It is the most widespread soil in the **Indo-Gangetic plains** but less common in the deep **Deccan** interior.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**:
 
 
• Develops on **crystalline igneous rocks** in areas of low rainfall. Its color is due to a wide diffusion of **Iron** in crystalline and metamorphic forms.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil**:
 
 
• Formed under conditions of **high temperature** and **heavy rainfall** with alternating wet and dry periods, leading to intense **leaching** of silica and lime.

questions.question: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) has increased the focus on which type of justice system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Victim-centric and restorative justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023** was enacted to replace the **Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860**, marking a paradigm shift from a **colonial-era retributive** approach to a modern framework prioritizing **justice** over mere **punishment**.
 
• The legislation introduces **community service** as a specific form of punishment for minor offenses (such as **defamation** and **public misconduct**), which is a core component of **restorative justice** aimed at offender reform.
 
• It empowers victims by mandating that they are informed of the **investigation progress** within **90 days**, ensuring their participation and right to information throughout the legal process.
 
• Specific provisions have been strengthened to protect **women and children**, including the introduction of **life imprisonment** or the **death penalty** for **gang rape** of minors, reflecting a **victim-centric** protection model.
 
• The **BNS** facilitates easier access to justice through the introduction of **Zero FIR** and **e-FIR**, allowing victims to report crimes irrespective of the **police station's jurisdiction**.

questions.question: In the Mansabdari system, what term referred to the cavalrymen maintained by the Mansabdar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sawar**__.

__
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was the administrative framework of the **Mughal Empire**, formalized by **Emperor Akbar** around **1571** to organize the nobility and the military.
 
• Under this system, every officer was assigned a **Mansab** (rank), which was divided into two distinct components: **Zat** and **Sawar**.
 
• The term **Sawar** referred to the specific number of **cavalrymen** or horsemen that a **Mansabdar** was mandated to maintain for imperial military service.
 
• The **Sawar** rank determined the military strength provided by the official and governed the allowance granted for the upkeep of **horses** and **troopers**.
 
• To ensure the quality of the **Sawar** contingent, the **Mughals** implemented the **Dagh** (branding of horses) and **Chehra** (descriptive rolls of soldiers) systems to prevent fraud and substitution.
 
• The **Sawar** rank could never exceed the **Zat** rank, and the ratio between the two determined the sub-class (first, second, or third) of the **Mansabdar** within their specific grade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zat**

 
 
• This indicated the **personal rank** and status of the officer in the imperial hierarchy.
 
• It was used to calculate the **personal salary** of the **Mansabdar**.
 
 
 
• **Jagir**
 
 
• These were **land revenue assignments** granted to **Mansabdars** in lieu of cash salaries.
 
• The holders, known as **Jagirdars**, collected revenue from these lands to cover their personal pay and the costs of their **Sawar** contingents.
 
 
 
• **Zamindar**
 
 
• Refers to hereditary **landed intermediaries** who had the right to collect land revenue from peasants.
 
• While **Zamindars** provided local stability and collected taxes, they were distinct from **Mansabdars**, who were appointed officials of the **Mughal state**.

⇒ 50³ = 50 × 50 × 50 = 125000

⇒ 20³ = 20 × 20 × 20 = 8000

⇒ 3 × 50 × 20 × 30 = 3 × 1000 × 30 = 90000

⇒ 125000 − 8000 − 90000

⇒ 117000 − 90000 = 27000

**∴ The correct answer is 27000.**

The cube of a sum is expanded as (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b).

Difference of Two Cubes

The factorization of the difference of two cubes is a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

questions.question: Average marks obtained by 15 boys is 55 (Each boy has obtained distinct value of marks). If the highest marks and lowest marks obtained are removed, then the average reduces by 1. What is the average of the highest and lowest marks obtained?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **Average** of **15 boys** = 55

After removing 2 boys, the **average reduces** to 54 (reduction of 1 per boy)

Sum of removed items (H + L) = (2 × Old Average) + (New Count × Reduction)

Sum of H + L = (2 × 55) + (13 × 1) = 110 + 13 = 123

Average of **highest** and **lowest** marks = 123 ÷ 2 = 61.5

**∴ The correct answer is 61.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of boys = 15

Initial **average marks** = 55

Number of boys after removing **highest** and **lowest** = 13

New average marks = 55 − 1 = 54

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc1983aa510682d5f247834d92e330e0d6bfa75063931d97b11201fb9b027d3d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of marks for 15 boys = 15 × 55 = 825

⇒ Total sum of marks for 13 boys = 13 × 54 = 702

⇒ Sum of marks of (Highest + Lowest) = 825 − 702 = 123

⇒ Average of (Highest + Lowest) = 123 ÷ 2 = 61.5

**∴ The correct answer is 61.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The **Arithmetic Mean** or average is the ratio of the sum of all observations to the total number of observations (Sum ÷ n).

Exclusion Principle

When values are removed from a group, the **sum of removed values** is equal to (Initial Total Sum) − (New Total Sum).

Impact on Average

If the **average reduces** after removing items, it means the average of the removed items was higher than the original average of the group.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio of 3 : 5. If the Highest Common Factor of the numbers is 18, then the sum of the numbers will be _____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **ratio parts** for the **sum** = 3 + 5 = 8 parts.

Since the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** represents the value of 1 unit in the ratio.

Sum of numbers = 8 × 18 = 144.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of two numbers = 3 : 5

**Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 18

**Formula Used:**

If the **ratio** of two numbers is a : b and their **HCF** is h, then the numbers are (a × h) and (b × h).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e9d8c40cfb3121dcf5fc416e7635693868bc6b27c2b1d7229e8c1ee996b1367.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 3x and 5x.

⇒ The **HCF** of 3x and 5x is x (since 3 and 5 are **coprime**).

⇒ Given x = 18.

⇒ First number = 3 × 18 = 54.

⇒ Second number = 5 × 18 = 90.

⇒ **Sum** of numbers = 54 + 90 = 144.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: A × B = HCF × LCM.

LCM from Ratio and HCF

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their HCF is h, then their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = a × b × h.

HCF of Coprime Numbers

If two numbers have no common factor other than 1, they are called **coprime** and their **HCF** is always 1.

questions.question: Six bells commence ringing together and ring at intervals of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 seconds respectively. In 20 minutes, how many times do they ring together? (including the first ringing together at commencement)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given intervals: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 seconds.

**LCM** (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30) = 300 seconds = **5 minutes**.

Number of times the bells ring together = (Total Time ÷ LCM) + 1.

Required times = (20 ÷ 5) + 1 = 4 + 1 = **5 times**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Intervals of six bells = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 seconds.

Total time duration = **20 minutes**.

**Formula Used:**

Common interval = **LCM** of individual intervals.

Number of rings = (Total duration ÷ Common interval) + 1 (to include the first ring).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ca3714949ee495155c7459d5ce232629227aff94e5d13ac021114b0336c0b6d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of intervals:

5 = 5

10 = 2 × 5

15 = 3 × 5

20 = 2² × 5

25 = 5²

30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3 × 5² = 4 × 3 × 25 = **300 seconds**.

⇒ Common interval in minutes = 300 ÷ 60 = **5 minutes**.

⇒ Total rings = (Total Duration ÷ Common Interval) + 1

⇒ Total rings = (20 ÷ 5) + 1 = 4 + 1 = **5 times**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. In coincidence problems (bells, traffic lights), the **LCM** determines the next time all events occur simultaneously.

Commencement Rule

When the problem states "including the first ring at commencement" or "ringing together at the start", always **add 1** to the division result: (Total Time ÷ Interval) + 1.

Unit Consistency

Before dividing, ensure the total time and the common interval are in the same unit (e.g., both in seconds or both in minutes).

questions.question: Ratio of the value of profit earned on an article to the selling price of the article is 3 : 8. What is the profit percentage?

Ratio of **Profit** to **Selling Price** = 3 : 8.

Let **Profit** = 3 units and **Selling Price** = 8 units.

**Cost Price** = 8 − 3 = 5 units.

**Profit Percentage** = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Profit** (P) to **Selling Price** (SP) = 3 : 8

**Formula Used:**

1) **Cost Price (CP)** = Selling Price − Profit

2) **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7557fa31ea72c7750c9a33d84279481a88a1ae2971a413fbf41608cab89efdd6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Profit** = 3x and **Selling Price** = 8x

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 8x − 3x

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 5x

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (3x ÷ 5x) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 0.6 × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

Loss percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Formula: Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Selling Price Calculation

When profit percentage is given: **Selling Price** = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This is a key ratio for solving **Markup** problems.

questions.question: Ratio of incomes of P and Q is 4 : 9 respectively. Ratio of expenditures of P and Q is 3 : 5 respectively. Savings of P is (1/6) of his income. What is the ratio of the savings of P and Q respectively?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Income of P** = 24 units → **Income of Q** = 54 units (Ratio 4 : 9).

**Savings of P** = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 units; **Expenditure of P** = 24 − 4 = 20 units.

Since **Expenditure ratio** is 3 : 5, **Expenditure of Q** = 20 × (5/3) = 100/3 units.

**Savings of Q** = **Income** − **Expenditure** = 54 − 100/3 = 62/3 units.

**Ratio of Savings** (P : Q) = 4 : (62/3) = 12 : 62 = 6 : 31.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Incomes** (P : Q) = 4 : 9

Ratio of **Expenditures** (P : Q) = 3 : 5

**Savings** of P = (1/6) × **Income** of P

**Formula Used:**

**Savings** = **Income** − **Expenditure**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4746a44930c96174b238b58a65732f54146b53eaa62060bdb579b70cacaeb7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Income of P** = 4x and **Income of Q** = 9x.

⇒ Let **Expenditure of P** = 3y and **Expenditure of Q** = 5y.

⇒ **Savings of P** = 4x − 3y

⇒ Given 4x − 3y = (1/6) × 4x

⇒ 4x − 3y = 2x/3

⇒ 3y = 4x − 2x/3 = 10x/3 ⇒ y = 10x/9

⇒ **Savings of Q** = 9x − 5y = 9x − 5 × (10x/9)

⇒ **Savings of Q** = (81x − 50x) / 9 = 31x/9

⇒ **Savings of P** = 4x − 3(10x/9) = 4x − 10x/3 = 2x/3

⇒ **Ratio of Savings** (P : Q) = (2x/3) : (31x/9) = 6 : 31.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings Relationship

The fundamental equation for financial aptitude is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any one component can be found if the other two are known or given in ratio form.

Ratio Scaling

When two different ratios are given (like Income and Expenditure), they cannot be compared directly unless a common variable or a specific condition (like Savings of P) relates them.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

The manager will fire the underperforming employees.

options.text: The underperforming employees must be fired by the manager.
The underperforming employees will fire the manager.
The underperforming employees will be fired by the manager.
The underperforming employees are fired by the manager.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The underperforming employees will be fired by the manager.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **Active Voice** and follows the structure of the **Simple Future Tense**: **Subject + will + V1 (base verb) + Object**.
 
• In this sentence, **The manager** is the **Subject**, **will fire** is the **Verb**, and **the underperforming employees** is the **Object**.
 
• To convert a **Simple Future Tense** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure used is: **New Subject (Object of active) + will + be + V3 (Past Participle) + by + New Agent (Subject of active)**.
 
• Following this rule, the object **the underperforming employees** moves to the subject position, and the verb **will fire** changes to **will be fired**.
 
• The original subject **the manager** is added at the end, preceded by the preposition **by**, resulting in the correct passive construction.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding why other options are incorrect based on **Tense** and **Modality**:
 
 
• **The underperforming employees must be fired by the manager**: This uses the modal verb **must**, which changes the degree of necessity and does not reflect the original **Simple Future** intent of **will**.
 
• **The underperforming employees will fire the manager**: This sentence remains in the **Active Voice** but reverses the **Subject** and **Object**, fundamentally altering the meaning of the original statement.
 
• **The underperforming employees are fired by the manager**: This structure represents the **Simple Present Tense** in passive voice (**is/am/are + V3**), failing to maintain the future timeframe established by **will**.
 
• In English grammar, the **Future Passive** is essential for formal reporting where the action or the receiver of the action is more significant than the performer.
 
 
</ul

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

The brothers decided to merge together their individual businesses to form one large company.

options.text: decided to together merge their individual businesses
decided to merge their individual businesses
decided to merge their individual businesses together

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decided to merge their individual businesses**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The primary error in the original sentence is **redundancy**. The verb **merge** is defined as the act of combining or joining two or more things to form a single entity. Therefore, the word **together** is already inherent in the definition of the word itself.

• Using **together** alongside **merge** creates a **pleonasm**, which is the use of more words than are necessary to convey a meaning. Removing the redundant word makes the sentence more **concise** and **grammatically precise**.

• The phrase **decided to merge their individual businesses** effectively communicates that the separate entities were joined into one without the linguistic clutter of unnecessary modifiers.

• In **formal English**, especially in a **business context**, it is essential to avoid repetitive phrasing to maintain professional clarity and flow.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Understanding Redundancy:**

• Redundant expressions occur when a modifier repeats the meaning of the word it modifies. Common examples in **competitive exams** include **revert back** (revert already means to go back), **advance forward** (advance already means to move forward), and **return back**.

• **Specific Contexts:**

• **Merge:** Rooted in the Latin **mergere**, meaning to dip or plunge. In **corporate law**, a **merger** is the legal consolidation of two entities into one.

• **Together:** While useful for emphasis in casual speech, it provides no new information when paired with verbs of **unification** like **combine**, **unite**, or **amalgamate**.

• **Sentence Improvement:** Option 1 is incorrect as it places the redundant word **together** between the infinitive marker and the verb, creating an awkward **split infinitive** structure. Option 3 simply moves the redundancy to the end of the clause.

</ul

questions.solution:
इसका सही उत्तर '**दीर्घकालिक नीति निर्माण**' है।

**__Key Points__**

**गद्यांश के अनुसार:**

__
 
• गद्यांश की पहली पंक्ति स्पष्ट रूप से बताती है कि आंतरिक सुरक्षा के क्षेत्र में **दीर्घकालिक नीति निर्माण** को तात्कालिक प्रतिक्रियाओं की तुलना में अधिक प्रभावी माना जाता है।
 
• **तात्कालिक प्रतिक्रियाएँ** अक्सर केवल वर्तमान स्थिति को संभालने के लिए होती हैं, जबकि दीर्घकालिक नीतियां भविष्य की चुनौतियों का सामना करने के लिए तैयार की जाती हैं।
 
• इसलिए, सही उत्तर **दीर्घकालिक नीति निर्माण** है।

**Additional Information__** **अन्य विकल्पों का विश्लेषण:**

**प्रशासनिक नियंत्रण:**

__
 
• यह सुरक्षा व्यवस्था का एक **कार्यान्वयन पक्ष** है, लेकिन गद्यांश में इसका उल्लेख प्रभावशीलता की तुलना के लिए नहीं किया गया है।

**दंड प्रक्रिया:**
